outputs.L4:
A conveyor for transporting people or goods between two landings includes a conveyance element extending in a longitudinal direction between the landings. The conveyance element may be formed, for example, by a sequence of steps, pallets, or a moving belt. At least one side of the conveyance element is bordered by a balustrade extending substantially along the direction of travel and separating the moving conveyance element from the surrounding area.

The conveyor further includes at least one presence sensor configured to detect a person or object within a defined detection zone. The sensor has a predetermined detection angle, detection range, and main detection direction. It may use optical, infrared, ultrasonic, radar, or another suitable sensing technology. Signals generated by the sensor can be supplied to a control unit that monitors activity near the conveyor and controls one or more operating functions.

The presence sensor is positioned at, on, within, or beside the balustrade so that its main detection direction faces away from the conveyance element. In this orientation, the detection zone extends into an area adjacent to the conveyor rather than being limited to the moving surface itself. The sensor can therefore detect people approaching, standing beside, or moving near the conveyor, including individuals who may not yet have stepped onto the conveyance element.

Information from the sensor may be used to start the conveyor, change its speed, maintain operation while a user is nearby, or initiate a warning or protective response. Multiple sensors may be arranged at different points along one or both balustrades to monitor selected areas near the landings or along the conveyor’s length. By directing the sensor outward from the balustrade, the system provides earlier and more reliable awareness of nearby people, enabling safer, more energy-efficient, and more responsive conveyor operation.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. Although it may seem insignificant, it plays an essential role in communication. As the definite article, “the” identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. For example, saying “the book” points to a specific book, while “a book” can refer to any book.

This simple word helps make sentences clear and precise. It allows speakers and writers to distinguish what is known from what is general. “The” can also add importance to a phrase, as in “the moment,” “the answer,” or “the future.”

Despite having only three letters, “the” demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can carry meaning, create context, and shape understanding.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent claim for a conveyor device with a moving conveyance element, side balustrade, and outward-facing person-detection sensor.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A conveyor device comprising:**  
a conveyance element configured to move along a conveyance path in a conveying direction;  
a balustrade disposed along a lateral side of the conveyance path and having an outward-facing side facing away from the conveyance path; and  
a person-detection sensor supported by the balustrade and having a detection field directed outwardly from the outward-facing side, the person-detection sensor being configured to generate a detection signal in response to detecting a person within the detection field.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for detecting people near an escalator or moving walkway, preserving reference numerals and defining the sensor’s detection direction, angles, and range.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention for detecting people near a passenger-transport installation comprises an escalator or moving walkway (1), an access region (2), and at least one contactless sensor (10) arranged adjacent to the access region (2). The sensor (10) detects a person (20) before the person reaches or leaves the moving conveying surface (3), and supplies a detection signal to a control unit (30), which may start, stop, slow, accelerate, or otherwise control the installation (1).

The sensor (10) has a detection direction (D) defined by a central detection axis extending from the sensor (10) toward the area in which approaching or departing people (20) are expected. A detection field (11) is formed around the detection direction (D). The field (11) is bounded horizontally by an azimuth angle (α) and vertically by an elevation angle (β). Detection occurs within a range (R) extending from a minimum distance (Rmin), which excludes objects immediately next to the sensor (10), to a maximum distance (Rmax), beyond which objects are disregarded.

The detection direction (D), angles (α, β), and range (Rmin–Rmax) are selected so that the detection field (11) covers the intended approach or departure zone (2) while substantially excluding the moving steps or pallets (3), adjacent traffic areas, and stationary structural components such as the balustrade (4). The sensor (10) may be a radar, lidar, ultrasonic, infrared, optical, or time-of-flight sensor. Multiple sensors (10) may be used to distinguish movement toward the installation (1) from movement away from it and to reduce false detections.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output: A conveyor device comprising a movable conveying surface configured to transport persons along a transport path, a balustrade disposed adjacent to at least one side of the conveying surface, and at least one sensor mounted at or proximate to the balustrade, the at least one sensor being configured to detect the presence or movement of a person within a detection zone extending outwardly away from the balustrade.
